clue.text: Overlook place that contains Smith Square?

parts.note: a forge is the workshop where a blacksmith works
T, as in a T-square, a drawing instrument for right angles

explanation.surface: Someone forgets the London address Smith Square, home of political headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Smith Square is a real Westminster address, but here 'Smith' is a blacksmith and 'Square' a T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget something is to neglect or fail to notice it, a synonym for overlook.

explanation.surface: A shipment of fine pottery arrives in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a left-arm wrist-spinner's ball is a rare type of bowl; and Josiah Wedgwood was a maker of fine porcelain, a china man.

parts.note: looks like darts, where a double is needed to start; read as a game that is top-class twice over, both words first and class meaning top

explanation.surface: A darts game that can only start once a player hits double twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts 'double top' is double twenty; here it means the two words of the answer each mean 'top'. A first-class match is a top-level cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-class match is cricket played at the highest domestic level, so a top-grade game.

clue.text: Bag taken to dance provides sport for ladies

parts.note: to bag something is to net it, as in netting a catch
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A woman takes her handbag to a dance, which gives her some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game played mainly by women, especially in British schools.

clue.text: Like Lee-Enfield in name, but not by design?

definitions.text: Like Lee-Enfield in name, but not by design?

parts.words: Like Lee-Enfield in name, but not by design?
parts.note: the rifle's hyphenated name has two parts, yet the gun itself has only one barrel

explanation.surface: A comment on the British Army's Lee-Enfield rifle and its naming.
explanation.walkthrough: A hyphenated surname like Lee-Enfield is called this, but the Lee-Enfield rifle is single-barrelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated surname is described as having two parts like a twin-barrelled shotgun.

parts.note: up means higher or above, as in being superior in position
an essay is an attempt, also called a shot

explanation.surface: The result of a top-grade school essay.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final result or consequence of something.

parts.note: aft means towards the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor touches a corpse at the back of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched in the old sense means slightly mad, which is what daft also means.

clue.text: Doctor taken to the tailless night-flier

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: the word 'the' loses its tail, its final letter

explanation.surface: A doctor is taken to see a nocturnal bird with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Most moths fly at night, unlike butterflies.

explanation.surface: Jewels smashed during a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds; and at a party guests break the ice to get conversation going.

clue.text: Annie, for example, something of an ectomorph, handicapped

annotationWithheld.why: Annie, for example, something of an ectomorph, handicapped: the run in 'ectomorph, handicapped' is ORPHHAN; only parse has 'handicapped' as both hidden-word text and the indicator removing its own H
annotationWithheld.clue: Annie, for example, something of an ectomorph, handicapped

parts.note: a public convenience, a men's toilet, is the gents in British English

explanation.surface: A toilet for sales reps.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of others, so they are representatives.

clue.text: See an American quail from short haircut-ghastly!

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
ghastly can mean deathly pale, as white as a sheet

explanation.surface: An exclamation of horror at a bird seen with an awful short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobwhite is a North American game bird of the quail family.

clue.text: They may score through the covers (especially on the first day)

definitions.text: They may score through the covers (especially on the first day)

parts.words: They may score through the covers (especially on the first day)
parts.note: sounds like batsmen scoring runs through the cricket covers field position; really people whose prized envelopes bear first-day postmarks

explanation.surface: Batsmen hitting runs through the covers early in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position; 'score' here means mark, as a postmark scores a stamp on a first-day cover envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelists prize first-day covers, envelopes franked on a stamp's first day of issue.

explanation.surface: Wasting away in a bunk bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay; and bunk, meaning nonsense, is also called rot.

parts.note: gains are profits
ay is an old or poetic word for always, also spelt aye

explanation.surface: Someone always denies making profits.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or dispute, a formal synonym.

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A crack in a church wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack shot or crack player is an expert, which is an ace.

parts.note: jumbo suggests the jet airliner, but means an elephant; its pilots are the drivers who ride it

explanation.surface: The aircrew of a jumbo jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahouts are Indian elephant drivers, who steer the beast like a pilot.

clue.text: Rash to be dismissed by 2, for example…

parts.note: a cricketer who is dismissed is out
the answer to 2 down is a ball that spins, so it is an example of a break, a ball that deviates

explanation.surface: A batsman is rashly out to an unusual delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down is CHINAMAN, a left-arm spinner's delivery that breaks (turns) off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of spots is a rash.

explanation.surface: An unusual delivery from an eccentric bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer of 2 down, CHINAMAN, an unusual delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: An unusual delivery in cricket is literally an odd ball; and an eccentric person is called an oddball.

clue.text: Second thoughts in respect of fee

parts.note: re means concerning or in respect of
a consideration is a payment or fee in legal language

explanation.surface: Thinking again about how much to charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking again about a decision is having second thoughts.

clue.text: Bad error, year short in model of solar system

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the word error are spoilt, put in a new order

parts.note: year cut short to its abbreviation Y

explanation.surface: A bad mistake leaves a year missing in a planetarium model.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model showing the planets orbiting the sun.

parts.note: the olive yields olive oil

explanation.surface: Is an oil company correct to back a stage musical?
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Bart's stage show based on Dickens's Oliver Twist is a famous musical.

clue.text: One of two posts one occupies on entering the house

definitions.text: One of two posts one occupies on entering the house

parts.words: One of two posts one occupies on entering the house
parts.note: sounds like jobs held in parliament; really the uprights either side of a front door you pass between

explanation.surface: A new MP holding two jobs on entering the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' and 'the house' suggest jobs and parliament; the posts are the upright sides of a door frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is one of the vertical side pieces of a door frame.

clue.text: Solemn people slow to come out

indicators.note: the letters of slow come out of order and are reworked

explanation.surface: Serious folk are slow to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are proverbially wise and grave-looking, so solemn people are called owls.

indicators.note: the following letter is missing from the word

parts.note: larking about means frolicking
G is the physics symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A poet larks about with no seriousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a twentieth-century English poet.

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters of circle are changed around

explanation.surface: A vicar who belongs to the Magic Circle, the British magicians' society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a London society of conjurors; 'Magic' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy.

explanation.surface: Being inclined to distort the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie is to be prone, lying flat; and to lie is to tell untruths.

clue.text: Loaded up, not having left port

indicators.note: not having left says the letter L, short for left, is removed

parts.note: laden means loaded

explanation.surface: A ship loaded up but unable to leave port.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen.
